items.stem: Which of the following best describes "solution"?
options: The filled symbol on a number line showing that the end value IS included (≤ or ≥)
The value of the unknown that makes an equation true
A statement that one quantity is less than (<), greater than (>), less than or equal to (≤) or greater than or equal to (≥) another

items.answer: The value of the unknown that makes an equation true
items.markingKey: B. "solution" is the value of the unknown that makes an equation true.

items.stem: Mohammed solves 3x − 3 = −3 and gets x = −2. By substituting, show that this is wrong, explain the error and find the correct solution.
items.answer: 3(−2) − 3 = −9 ≠ −3; Mohammed subtracted 3 instead of adding it. Correct: x = 0.

items.stem: Explain the difference between x < 4 and x ≤ 4.
items.answer: x < 4 does not include 4 (open circle) while x ≤ 4 includes 4 (closed circle).

items.stem: Explain why the steps for solving 2x + 3 = 11 are "subtract 3, then divide by 2".
items.answer: x was multiplied by 2 and then 3 was added; the inverse operations are applied in reverse order.

items.stem: Explain why the equation 3(x + 7) = 3x + 28 has no solution.
items.answer: 3x + 21 = 3x + 28 gives 21 = 28, which is false for every x.
items.markingKey: Expansion (M1); contradiction identified (R1).

items.stem: Explain why you should define what your letter stands for when forming an equation.
items.answer: Stating "let n be the number of tickets" makes the meaning of the equation and its solution clear to the reader.

items.stem: Sofia writes: "x > 2 is shown with a closed circle at 2." Explain why this is inaccurate.
items.answer: x > 2 does not include 2, so it uses an open circle.

items.stem: Yusuf solves 8x − 4 = −20 and gets x = −3. By substituting, show that this is wrong, explain the error and find the correct solution.
items.answer: 8(−3) − 4 = −28 ≠ −20; Yusuf subtracted 4 instead of adding it. Correct: x = −2.
items.markingKey: Substitution shows the error (M1); wrong inverse operation identified (R1); correct solution (A1).

items.stem: Mateo thinks of a number, multiplies it by 7, then subtracts 10. The result is 130. (a) Write an equation and solve it to find the number. (b) Show that "multiply by 7 and subtract 10" can be undone by "add 10 and divide by 7" for any starting number.
items.markingKey: (a) 7n − 10 = 130, n = 20 (b) (7n − 10 + 10)/7 = 7n/7 = n. Equation formed from the context (M1 A1); solved with inverse operations (M1 A1); interpreted/justified (D/B: R1).

items.stem: The perimeter of a rectangle is the same as the perimeter of an equilateral triangle. The rectangle measures (x + 4) cm by (2x − 1) cm and each side of the triangle is (x + 7) cm. (a) Form and solve an equation. (b) Find the perimeter. (c) Check that all lengths are positive.
items.markingKey: (a) 2(x + 4) + 2(2x − 1) = 3(x + 7) ⇒ 6x + 6 = 3x + 21, x = 5 (b) 36 cm (c) sides 9, 9, 12 cm, all positive. Equation set up with brackets (M1 A1); solved (M1 A1); answer checked or interpreted in context (D: R1).

items.stem: Rafael is 8 years older than Nia. In 3 years’ time Rafael will be twice as old as Nia. (a) Let Nia’s age now be x and form an equation. (b) Solve it. (c) Check your answer in the words of the problem.
items.answer: (a) x + 8 + 3 = 2(x + 3) (b) x = 5 (c) now 5 and 13; in 3 years 8 and 16 ✓
items.markingKey: (a) x + 8 + 3 = 2(x + 3) (b) x = 5 (c) now 5 and 13; in 3 years 8 and 16 ✓. Unknown defined and equation formed (M1 A1); solved (M1 A1); checked/interpreted in context (D: R1 C1).

items.stem: Elena has €120 to spend at a fair in Lisbon. Entry is €9 and each ride costs €7. (a) Write an inequality for the number of rides r. (b) Solve it. (c) What is the greatest number of rides, and how much money is left over?
items.markingKey: (a) 9 + 7r ≤ 120 (b) r ≤ 111/7 (c) 15 rides, €6 left. Inequality formed (M1 A1); solved (A1); integer answer interpreted in context (R1); number line/notation correct (C1).
